title: End-to-end architecture
task_statement: Design a Claude application with named stages, trust boundaries, state in the application, and a trace for each stage. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Request loop with state in the application
components.first_principle: No state persists between Messages API calls. The application resends the conversation on each call and checks each stop reason.
steps: Send the full conversation history with each Messages API request.
Read the stop_reason field before you accept the response.
Run each requested tool in your code and return a tool_result block.
Repeat the request while stop_reason is tool_use.
Handle max_tokens, refusal, and pause_turn as separate outcomes.
Log the stage name and the token counts for each call.
pros: The request carries its full state, so a run can be replayed from stored inputs. (Inference)
The stop reasons give a documented exit condition for the loop.
The application controls each retry and each fallback. (Inference)
cons: The application sends more tokens as the history grows. (Inference)
The team owns the state store and its failure modes. (Inference)
Each stop reason needs a handler, or the loop fails without a clear cause. (Inference)
use_when: A multi-turn conversation needs context from earlier turns.
A tool call must return to your code before the next model turn.
The team needs to replay a run from stored inputs. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: One prompt and one answer need no history and no tools. (Inference)
A managed session already stores the state, and the team accepts its controls. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Log each stop reason with a count per request. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Alert when the counts for max_tokens or refusal rise. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Stream the response when the user waits for the first tokens.
constraints.combination: Use fine-grained tool streaming when the tool input must appear early.

constraints.choice: Use the Message Batches API for bulk work that does not need an immediate answer.
Keep each conversation state scoped to one user or tenant. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D1.2. Expect a stem with a failure that no stage can explain. The credited answer adds a trace for each stage and a named gate. (Inference)
components.trap: A larger model or a longer prompt for a failure that no trace locates. The change treats a symptom and hides the stage that breaks. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Keep the history, the retries, and the stop reason handling in application code.
components.exam_tip: If a stem shows a failure with no known stage, pick the option that adds a trace per stage. (Inference)

key_facts.text: The Messages API is stateless, so you always send the full conversational history.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The tool-use loop exits on end_turn, max_tokens, stop_sequence, or refusal.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: A pause_turn stop reason means the work is not complete, and you send the conversation again.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The Agent SDK exports traces, metrics, and events with OpenTelemetry.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The docs state that model behavior is not a security control.
key_facts.label: Fact

components.name: Verification and output gates
components.first_principle: A check in code compares the draft with the source and the schema before the answer leaves the system. (Inference)
steps: Request structured outputs when the answer must match a schema.
Check the parsed output against the schema in code.
Compare each factual claim with the source record in code.
Run an output guard that blocks restricted content.
Send each failed draft to a hold queue, not to the user.
Log the check result for each draft.
pros: A hold queue stops a wrong draft before it reaches the user. (Inference)
Code checks add no model tokens. (Inference)
cons: Schema compliance does not show that the values are correct. (Inference)
Strict checks reject correct answers that fall outside the rule set. (Inference)
Each gate adds latency and one more failure point. (Inference)
use_when: A wrong value triggers a payment, a data change, or an action that a patient sees. (Inference)
A downstream system needs an object with a fixed schema.
Each claim in the output must trace to a source document. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: The output is free text with no downstream system and low risk. (Inference)
No source record exists to compare against. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Use the inference_geo parameter where data residency rules apply.
constraints.combination: On Claude Platform on AWS, requests with inference_geo on Claude Haiku 4.5 return a 400 error.

constraints.choice: Route each failed draft to a named reviewer. (Inference)
Track the rate of failed checks for each stage. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Alert when the rate rises after a prompt change. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Run checks in code, so that only the model call adds token cost. (Inference)

native_services.text: Not in source for platform-specific schema support.

components.exam_tie: D1.2. Expect a stem with a financial or safety-critical output. The credited answer places a deterministic check between the draft and the user. (Inference)
components.trap: A prompt that asks the model to check its own draft. The check shares the failure mode of the draft, so it gives no independent control. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Use a check in code for each output whose error costs money, safety, or trust.
components.exam_tip: If a stem names a schema, pick structured outputs, and add a code check for the values. (Inference)

key_facts.text: Structured outputs guarantee schema-compliant responses, because the model output is limited to the schema.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Strict tool use guarantees schema validation on tool names and inputs.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The docs state that Claude is inherently resilient to prompt injection, but model behavior is not a security control.
key_facts.label: Fact

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Output reaches a user or system?} -->|No| X[Single call may be enough]
  A -->|Yes| B{Error cost high?}
  B -->|No| C[Trace each stage and sample]
  B -->|Yes| D{Schema needed?}
  D -->|Yes| E[Structured outputs plus code check]
  D -->|No| F[Code check on each claim]
  E --> G[Hold queue for failures]
  F --> G
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  U[User input] --> V[Validate in code]
  V --> S[Application state]
  S --> M[Messages API call]
  M --> R{stop_reason}
  R -->|tool_use| T[Run tools]
  T --> S
  R -->|end_turn| K[Check output in code]
  K --> O[Answer or hold]
